title: Schema migration runner for the orders database
name: Orders migration runner

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this runner protects the schema from concurrent or partially applied migrations? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two replicas of the service start at the same moment against an empty database. What happens?
choices: Both run migration 1 concurrently; the primary key on schema_migrations makes one of them fail and exit.
One replica takes the advisory lock and migrates; the other blocks in pg_advisory_lock, then finds every version already applied and applies nothing.
Both replicas apply all migrations, because CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS makes each statement idempotent.
The second replica gets an immediate error from pg_advisory_lock and Up returns without migrating.

questions.prompt: Migration 2 runs on a database where existing rows violate the new reserved_within_stock constraint. What is the state afterwards?
choices: The reserved column exists but the constraint is missing, and version 2 is recorded as applied.
The reserved column exists and version 2 is not recorded, so the next start fails on 'column already exists'.
Neither the column, the constraint nor a schema_migrations row for version 2 exists; version 1 stays applied.
Everything from versions 1 and 2 is rolled back because the runner uses one transaction for the whole Up call.

questions.prompt: An engineer fixes a typo inside the SQL of migration 3 after it has already been deployed everywhere. What happens on the next start?
choices: The runner re-executes migration 3 with the new SQL on top of the existing index.
The new SQL is ignored because version 3 is already recorded; startup continues normally.
The runner updates the stored checksum to the new value and continues.
Up stops with an error naming migration 3 and no further migrations are attempted.
